scope: Corollary 8.1 (Endomorphisms and continuous flows) of the manuscript “Rokhlin's multiple-mixing problem for one transformation” (preprints/Rokhlins-multiple-mixing-problem-for-one-transformation-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 145 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 45000cec6bcec95d), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 38. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let (Ω, F, µ) be an arbitrary probability space. 1. Suppose T : Ω → Ω is measurable, preserves µ, and µ(A ∩ T−nB) → µ(A)µ(B) as n → +∞ for every A, B ∈ F. Then, for every fixed k ≥ 2 and measurable A1, . . . , Ak, µ k \ i=1 T−ti Ai ! −→ k Y i=1 µ(Ai) along nonnegative integer times t1 < · · · < tk whose least successive gap tends to infinity. Only preimages under forward iterates are used. 2. Let (St)t∈R be a probability-preserving group of invertible measurable transformations. Assume µ(A ∩ S−1 t B) → µ(A)µ(B) as t → +∞ for every A, B ∈ F, and that its Koopman operators Utf = f ◦ St are strongly continuous on L1(µ); equivalently, ∥Us1A − 1A∥1 −→ 0 (s → 0) for every A ∈ F. The same product limit holds with T−ti Ai replaced by S−1 ti Ai and with arbitrary real times t1 < · · · < tk whose least successive gap tends to infinity.
